title: finding(docs-census): the `const schema = {` census spelling over-counts prose and under-counts by identifier — the instrument has the same defect as the class
body:
## Observation

The census spelling this repository uses to size the "bare `const schema = {` literal" class is keyed to the **identifier**, and it is a **whole-file** grep. Both properties bite:

```
git grep -c "const schema = {"   over content/docs/**
```

- **It over-counts prose.** Two of its 28 hits on `origin/main` are sentences **outside any fence**, and — measured, not paraphrased — both sentences are arguments *for* annotating:

  > `content/docs/plugins/plugin-form.mdx:394` — "…so an un-annotated `const schema = { … }` type-checks whatever is written in it, while `const signUpForm: FormSchema` makes a wrong `validation` shape a compile error."
  >
  > `content/docs/plugins/plugin-grid.mdx:612` — "Annotating the literal is the point: an un-annotated `const schema = { … }` type-checks no matter what is written in it…"

  ⭐ The instrument counted its own justification as its own population. ⇒ Real code population **26 across 11 pages**, not the 28/13 the grep reports.

- **It under-counts by identifier.** A bare schema literal written under any other name is invisible to it. Eight such occurrences exist in `content/docs`: `blocks/index.mdx:71`, `guide/schema-rendering.md:367,370,371,372,374`, `plugins/plugin-markdown.mdx:178,208`.

## Why this is filed as an observation and not as work

⚠️ The eight are **not** a ready-made sweep. Several are prose sketches of the `{ /* ... */ }` shape that could never be annotated, so the actionable subset is smaller than 8 and wants a triage reading before anyone touches it. Sizing it here would be doing the grading this seat does not do.

⭐ And the load-bearing point is not the arithmetic. It is that **this class's own measuring instrument has the same defect the class has**: a whole-file grep cannot answer a question that is about one region of a file. objectui#8125's sweep hit it, objectui#8047's `it(`-anchored sweep hit the mirror image of it (it under-counts by 32 *and* over-reports a prose `it (`), and this seat has hit it three times today on landing probes — a docblock, a different schema, and a deliberately dated historical sentence, each matching a pattern the probe predicted would return zero.

⇒ Whatever the next reader does with the eight, the durable answer is that a population claim about fenced code should be measured **through the fence walker**, the way `check-doc-snippet-types` already does, ⛔ not with a repo-wide `git grep`.

⛔ No fix is proposed and none is owed. ⛔ This card asserts no priority and no domain — filed for triage's first grading, per the protocol that `domain:*` and grading are produced by the triage seat alone.

## Provenance and the dedupe

Measured by the objectui#8125 dev while sweeping, and handed to this seat **unfiled** because both of that seat's dedupe channels were down: REST `/search/issues` returns 403 by design, and MCP `search_issues` failed twice with a rate-limit naming **another account's** user ID (this session's own quota read 15000/15000 core and 10000/10000 graphql). ⇒ Filing blind and dropping the finding are both forbidden, so it came here.

Dedupe run by this seat instead: the newest 323 issues (open **and** closed, 6 REST pages, paginated on raw page size) with objectui#8047 and objectui#8483 as known-present controls — both hit. The only title match for this class is objectui#8125 itself. ⚠️ The sibling finding handed over in the same batch **was** a duplicate (of objectui#8310) and was therefore **not** filed — the corroboration went onto that card instead. This one is not.
